endings.title: The Steady Light
endings.summary: Permanent restoration: the repaired route passed its physical checks and the separate endpoint service test.
scene: The beacon above the Iron Threshold settles into a steady glow. For once, the enormous gate has nothing to complain about. You close the test record, leaving the observations beside the conclusion where the next engineer can find them.

Below, the Rift is still a scar in the stone. It is no longer an excuse for an outage. The Underworld has a working connection and a record of how you proved it. Beyond the gate, the Iron City keeps its own unfinished chapter.
endings.continuation: Continue returns to the safe Iron Threshold. Earlier rooms remain available. The Iron City is a future episode boundary, not a missing puzzle.

endings.title: The Borrowed Dawn
endings.summary: Temporary restoration: the borrowed bypass passed its physical checks and the separate endpoint service test. A temporary dependency remains.
scene: The beacon lights, and someone has the good sense to leave the temporary-route sign standing. Dawn has arrived on borrowed equipment. It is still dawn.

You leave two lines in the handover: service restored; permanent work outstanding. The second line is not a smaller victory. It is the reason tomorrow's engineer will know what to do before the borrowed installation must go home.
endings.continuation: Continue returns to the safe Iron Threshold. The borrowed installation remains a temporary dependency; earlier rooms are still available.

endings.title: The Honest Shutdown
endings.summary: Deliberate safe shutdown: the severed conduit remains disconnected and service is unresolved. Isolation is not restoration.
scene: The beacon stays dark. You hang a clear fault notice where a hopeful guess used to be. Even the enormous gate seems relieved to receive an honest answer.
The chapter closes with the damaged path isolated and the next work written down. There will be no celebration of a repair that has not happened. There can still be a next attempt.
endings.continuation: Continue returns to safe encounter preparation in this temporary session. Preparation and inventory rewind; new clues, personal notes and hint-use history remain. Earlier measurements become stale and must be repeated.

routes.copper: Your record follows the copper route through the Warrens and Echo Cavern. The pages distinguish an intact conductor path from a powered device that merely looks busy.
routes.fiber: Your record follows the fiber route through the Photon Gardens and Prism Vault. Inspection, compatibility and measured loss share the page; a bright-looking path never stood in for those checks.
routes.radio: Your record follows the radio route through the Skywell and Storm Observatory. Signal and noise have separate places in the notebook. Neither was allowed to make a promise about service by itself.
routes.none: The gate ledger has a line for the repair route. You leave it blank. The conduit is safely isolated, and the next engineer still has a choice.

noAllies: You faced the Rift with your own observations and a well-used toolkit.

sideQuests.text: At the Antique Serial Post, you helped the Ancient Tortoise deliver the short message. The handover remembers a small successful delivery as well as the larger interruption.
You helped Electric Eel complete the energy audit and identify the over-budget plan. That separate piece of careful work belongs in the record too.
Your completed Skywell Weather Diary keeps two observations apart in time. The sky was allowed to change its mind; the notebook kept both entries.

You reunited three notebook records: the Copper Warrens’ documented break, the Photon Gardens’ connector inspection, and the Shell Market’s delivered-power ledger. The recovered maintenance history preserves each source. It does not establish when earlier repairs happened, who performed them, or whether a current path or service works.

noSideQuests: The main journey has a chapter of its own.

maintenance.recorded: The borrowed-route handover stays tucked into your notebook, its limits and follow-up plainly marked.

recovery.retry: Retry from Encounter Preparation is temporary session recovery, not a second save slot. Preparation and inventory rewind together. New clues, personal notes and hint-use history remain; earlier measurements become stale. Save later at an ordinary safe moment to keep that learning across sessions.
recovery.restore: Restore Save loads the signed-in account's one saved snapshot. It replaces this in-memory adventure and its unsaved changes; it does not retain new learning from this attempt. Review that decision before loading.
recovery.guest: Guests can retry from the in-memory preparation checkpoint. Sign in before checking or loading an account save; signing in alone does not restore it.
recovery.save: This scene does not overwrite your account save. Terminal failure and unresolved shutdown cannot be saved or autosaved.

hazard.choice: Cross the marked unstable inspection ledge
hazard.warning: DANGER: beyond the work-zone barrier, the unsupported inspection ledge can collapse into the excavation trench and kill the apprentice. Crossing is optional and never required for a repair. Stay on the safe platform to inspect the conduit. Your account save will remain unchanged.
hazard.acknowledgement: I understand that crossing the unstable ledge can kill the apprentice
hazard.safeAlternative: Stay on the safe inspection platform
hazard.title: A Shortcut Too Short
scene: You step beyond the barrier. The clay shelf parts from the trench wall with the weary sigh of something that was never a bridge.
Your adventure ends in the Rift. The Backhoe of Doom lowers its bucket like a hat. The sign, regrettably, was doing its job.
hazard.cause: The unsupported inspection ledge collapsed after you chose to cross the marked barrier. The fall killed the apprentice. This is a fictional story hazard, not the result of an incorrect diagnosis. Safe inspection from the platform avoids it.
